name: Video Codec Analysis
description: Examines video encoding patterns and codec artifacts to detect re-encoding and manipulation traces.
useCase: Detecting video tampering through codec fingerprint and encoding history analysis
mechanism: Analyzes video container metadata, codec parameters, quantization patterns, and encoding artifacts. Manipulated videos often show signs of re-encoding (double compression artifacts), mismatched codec parameters, or encoding patterns inconsistent with claimed source devices.
accuracy: Medium-High - 73-85% on re-encoded and manipulated videos
source: Stamm, M. et al. (2012) - Anti-Forensics of Digital Image Compression, IEEE TIFS
algorithm: Container Analysis + Codec Parameter Extraction + Double Compression Detection + Encoding Pattern Matching
parameters: Codecs: H.264/H.265/VP9/AV1, QP analysis: block-level, GOP structure: reference frame pattern
strengths:
• Detects re-encoding manipulation traces
• Works on any video format
• Non-content-dependent analysis
• Fast processing (metadata-level analysis)
limitations:
• Original codec info may be stripped
• Multiple legitimate re-encodings confuse analysis
• Streaming platforms always re-encode
• New codecs may not be supported

references.title: Stamm, M. et al. (2012). Anti-Forensics of Digital Image Compression. IEEE TIFS.
Jiang, X. et al. (2013). In-Loop and Out-of-Loop Filter Decision Detection in HEVC Compressed Video. IEEE SPL.
Vazquez-Padin, D. et al. (2020). Detection of Video Double Encoding with GOP Size Estimation. WIFS.
